subject.title: Vertex beta INVALID_ARGUMENT can wedge long sessions without actionable recovery

question: Should generic LiteLLM/Vertex beta 400 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` errors without token-limit, tool-turn, image, or thinking-signature wording trigger automatic session recovery/fallback, or only actionable messaging plus redacted logs?
rationale: Current source intentionally classifies narrower provider rejection shapes and leaves generic invalid-argument text generic; changing this affects provider failover, session-state recovery, and the risk of hiding real request schema defects.

options.title: Narrow provider recovery after live proof
options.body: Classify only the verified LiteLLM Vertex beta error shape and prove the failed turn releases or repairs the session lane without hiding unrelated schema errors.

options.title: Actionable message only
options.body: Surface a clearer provider-rejected-request message and log details while avoiding automatic reset/fallback for ambiguous 400s.

options.title: Fold into provider-rejection design
options.body: Make a broader provider-rejected-history/session recovery effort canonical and close this only after that design explicitly covers LiteLLM Vertex beta.

recommendation.title: Narrow provider recovery after live proof
recommendation.body: Classify only the verified LiteLLM Vertex beta error shape and prove the failed turn releases or repairs the session lane without hiding unrelated schema errors.
